clue.text: Laughed at being put away

definitions.meaning: to laugh at someone is to mock or jeer at them
food that is put away has been eaten greedily

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: mocked with derision, and wolfed down as food eaten hungrily.

clue.text: Organ producing bile?

parts.note: an organ of the body that, in its figurative sense, stands for bad temper or venom rather than digestive fluid

explanation.walkthrough: The liver makes actual bile; the question mark warns that this organ's bile is the figurative kind, irritable spite.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdominal organ near the stomach has a long-standing figurative meaning of anger or ill humour, bile in its emotional sense.

clue.text: Whitstable resident making way into hall, topless

indicators.note: into says the road abbreviation goes inside the trimmed entrance hall
topless means the first letter of the word for the hall is dropped

parts.note: a foyer is an entrance hall
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone from the Kent town is making their way into a hall without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitstable is a Kent seaside town famous for its shellfish beds, so its 'resident' lives in the sea, not a house; 'topless' leaves OYER for 'into' to fill.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish is the town's most famous inhabitant, harvested from the beds off its coast.

clue.text: It is, in passing, an unreliable thing

definitions.text: It is, in passing, an unreliable thing

parts.words: It is, in passing, an unreliable thing
parts.note: read literally, something moving past after dark; as an idiom, a shady person or business not to be trusted

explanation.walkthrough: The literal reading of the phrase is travelling past through the dark, which 'in passing' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated phrase describes a dodgy, untrustworthy person or outfit that may vanish suddenly.

clue.text: Money, they say, is needed to get a rise

definitions.meaning: slang for cash, as people commonly call it

definitions.text: is needed to get a rise
definitions.meaning: a bread mix that swells with yeast before baking

explanation.definitionFit: It is slang for cash and also the yeasted mixture that rises before being baked into bread.

clue.text: Killer's wrath dividing rural establishment

indicators.note: dividing says the anger word splits the farm word in two

parts.note: a farm is an establishment in the countryside
ire means wrath

explanation.surface: A murderer's fury splits up a country farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividing' puts IRE between F and ARM; the 's on 'Killer' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun is a weapon that kills, so it can be called a killer.

clue.text: Old mathematician's story on witchcraft not beginning to be written up

parts.note: a fib is a story, a small lie
taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, written up means the letters run upwards, so read backwards
not beginning says the first letter of the witchcraft word is dropped

parts.note: Wicca is a modern form of witchcraft

explanation.surface: A tale about an old mathematician involving sorcery that has not begun to be recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not beginning' drops W from WICCA to give ICCA, and 'written up' turns that to ACCI.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo of Pisa, known by this name, was a medieval Italian mathematician famous for his number sequence.

clue.text: Off-line?

definitions.meaning: food that is off is rotten or foul-smelling
a row of soldiers standing side by side

explanation.definitionFit: The word means foul-smelling, like food gone off, and also a row of soldiers or a line of taxis.

clue.text: Rigorous process, biting banker

parts.note: acid remarks are biting, sharp
a banker is something with banks, a river: the Test is a river in Hampshire

explanation.surface: A bank official's teeth in a coin make for a tough examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' suggests money but is the crossword's river; the Test is a famous trout river in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a decisive, severe trial, from the use of nitric acid to assay gold.

clue.text: Radio's visual display making wonderful dotted character audible

parts.note: magic as an adjective means wonderful

indicators.note: audible means the letter is to be heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: the small letter i is the character written with a dot

explanation.surface: A radio's screen makes a marvellous dotted letter heard.
explanation.walkthrough: A small i carries a dot; said out loud it is the same as EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: An old valve radio's tuning indicator was a glowing tube called by this name.

clue.text: Healthy, though out of practice with different side

indicators.note: different side says right is swapped for left, the other side

parts.note: rusty means out of practice

explanation.surface: Fit and well, though a bit rusty playing on the other wing.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) in RUSTY is swapped for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means vigorous and robustly healthy.

clue.text: Constant keeping British resolute

indicators.note: keeping says the word for constant holds the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: unending means constant, never stopping

explanation.surface: Steadfast and keeping British, a person stays resolute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constant' looks like the definition at the start, but it is the outer wordplay; the definition is 'resolute' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who will not bend is firm and determined, resolute.

clue.text: Cooker, hob, dishwasher, washing machine, fridge freezer etc etc?

definitions.text: Cooker, hob, dishwasher, washing machine, fridge freezer etc etc?

parts.words: Cooker, hob, dishwasher, washing machine, fridge freezer etc etc?
parts.note: a list of all the kitchen appliances one could take, short of the plumbing fixture under the window, the idiom for taking absolutely all

explanation.walkthrough: The long list plus 'etc etc' paints the idiom: every item except the one fixture still plumbed in.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means absolutely all of something, and this list of appliances is all a kitchen holds bar one fixture.

clue.text: See edges taken off by the ears

indicators.note: edges taken off means the first and last letters of the word for see are removed

parts.note: to notice is to see

explanation.surface: Someone sees the edges of something removed near the ears.
explanation.walkthrough: NOTICE loses its first and last letters, N and E.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective is the medical term for relating to the ear, so by or of the ears.

clue.text: Put your glad rags on and hurry up about it!

definitions.meaning: glad rags are smart clothes, so dress smartly
be quick, get a move on

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means appear smartly dressed, and as an order it means be quick about it.

clue.text: Safely home, confounding you on clues, though not the last in puzzle

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: confounding means mixing up, so the letters are rearranged
though not says a letter is to be left out of the fodder
the last in picks out the final letter of the word puzzle

explanation.surface: Safely home, having confounded you on clues, except the end of the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The E comes from 'the last in puzzle', and 'not' strikes it from the fodder before 'confounding' does its work; 'home' is the usual crossword IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Done harmlessly, without causing injury, means done in a safe way.

clue.text: Old US whaling centre's article on food caught?

annotationWithheld.why: Old US whaling centre's article on food caught? (9): AN + TUCK inside NET would need 'caught' to be both NET and the container signal, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Old US whaling centre's article on food caught?

clue.text: Empty locker in small hole in ceiling

indicators.note: in says the emptied key goes inside the word for small

parts.note: slight means small

indicators.note: empty means the inner letter of the word for locker is taken out

parts.note: a key is something that locks, a locker

explanation.surface: An empty cupboard sits in a small hole in the ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: A locker suggests a cupboard but is a key, which locks; 'Empty' removes its middle E to leave KY.
explanation.definitionFit: A window set into a roof or ceiling is an opening letting in light.

clue.text: Reported evidence of locusts overhead in the 1920s?

indicators.note: reported signals the words are said aloud, giving a sound-alike phrase

parts.note: locusts leave an eaten crop behind them

explanation.surface: Signs of a locust plague were noted in the skies in the 1920s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overhead' looks like the sky the locusts fill, but means on the head: a short hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A severely short bob for women was fashionable in the 1920s, a style worn on top of the head.

clue.text: See 11
See 11
Not entirely keen on providing actor

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter of the word for keen is cut off

parts.note: a keen blade is sharp
if means providing, on condition that

explanation.surface: Not wholly enthusiastic about supplying a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: SHARP loses its last letter to give SHAR; Omar Sharif was the Egyptian star of Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Omar Sharif was a film actor, so the surname stands for an actor.

clue.text: Cat's course in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means as heard in speech, a sound-alike

parts.note: links is a golf course by the sea

explanation.surface: A cat's path is a topic of chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a golf course, LINKS, which is said the same as the cat's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears.

clue.text: As expected, sigh about dish, having removed lid

indicators.note: about says the word for sigh goes round the dish

parts.note: a sough is a sighing or murmuring sound, as of wind

indicators.note: having removed lid means the first letter of the dish is dropped

parts.note: a tureen is a serving dish for soup

explanation.surface: Predictably, someone sighs over a dish after taking its lid off.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUGH is a rare word for the sighing of wind; 'having removed lid' takes the first letter off the soup dish, leaving UREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means just as predicted, indeed, as one expected.

clue.text: Dash into hospital, cellulite on the up

indicators.note: on the up says the hidden letters are read backwards
into says the letters are found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rush into hospital over cellulite that is getting worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Dash into' as the definition, but 'into' signals the hidden run; ECLAT means dash or flair alone. In a down clue 'on the up' reads TALCE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean showy brilliance or flair, a striking stylish effect.

clue.text: Big sport, nothing to add?

parts.note: to sum is to add up
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A heavyweight game where there's nothing more to say.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because Japanese wrestlers are famously huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese wrestling is fought by very heavy wrestlers, so it is a big men's sport.

clue.text: Art of black dance music in large convertible

indicators.note: in says the music genre goes inside the rearranged letters
convertible means able to be changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: funk is a style of dance music from black American musicians

explanation.surface: The art of black dance music played in a big open-topped car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' looks like painting but is Art Garfunkel of Simon and Garfunkel; 'convertible' turns the letters of 'large' into GAREL.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Garfunkel is the singer, so his surname goes with the first name Art.

clue.text: He's had issue with half-hearted sales talk

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the two middle letters is removed

parts.note: patter is glib sales talk

explanation.surface: A man with a problem about weak sales talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring, not a problem; PATTER has two T's at its heart, and losing one halves it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for father, used in schoolboy slang, means a man who has had children, issue.

clue.text: Garment to touch lightly, minding business

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: minding means looking after, holding the business abbreviation within

parts.note: to pat is to touch lightly
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A coat for touching gently while minding the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minding' looks like paying attention, but here means holding something in its care, so it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcoat worn on top of other clothes is an outer garment.

clue.text: Felt shy about old solver's inward reference

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling shy about someone's private thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver is 'you', so an archaic reference back to the solver is the old reflexive pronoun, as in 'know thyself'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic reflexive pronoun for you, as addressed to the solver, means yourself.
